title: Riders at the Gate
text: Five riders wait at the gate under the Salt King's banner. Their captain wants a share of the granary, for what he calls the protection of the road.

choices.label: Pay them
choices.chronicle: {When}, riders of the Salt King came to the gate, and the house paid them a tithe of grain.

choices.label: Offer them a meal instead

yes.chronicle: The captain laughed, but he ate, and he rode away without the grain.

no.chronicle: They ate the meal, then took the grain anyway.

choices.chronicle: {When}, riders of the Salt King came to the gate, and {abbot} invited them to eat in the refectory.

choices.label: Refuse them

yes.chronicle: On their way out they fired the woodpile.

no.chronicle: They rode away laughing, and promised to come back.

choices.chronicle: {When}, riders of the Salt King demanded grain at the gate, and {abbot} refused them.

title: The Riders Return
text: As some of the brothers had warned, the Salt King's riders are back. The captain says the road has grown more dangerous, and the price has gone up.

choices.label: Pay again
choices.chronicle: {When}, the Salt King's riders came back for more grain, and were paid again.

choices.label: Not this time
choices.chronicle: {When}, the Salt King's riders came back for more, and this time {abbot} sent them away empty-handed.

effects.chronicle: {When}, {monk} was found on the road below the house, beaten and left in the ditch. Everyone knew who had done it.

title: Someone Takes the Wood
text: For three nights running, firewood has gone missing from the stack by the wall.

choices.label: Set a watch through the night

yes.chronicle: The watch caught a widow and her two sons with their arms full of wood. They were fed, and sent home with a bundle.

no.chronicle: The watch saw nothing, and the wood kept going.

choices.chronicle: {When}, someone was stealing from the woodpile.

choices.label: Leave a bundle by the gate for whoever needs it
choices.chronicle: {When}, wood began to vanish from the stack, and {abbot} ordered a bundle left by the gate each night for whoever needed it.

title: A Family at the Gate
text: A family with a handcart waits at the gate: a man, his wife, and a small girl wrapped in a blanket who has not stopped coughing.

choices.label: Take them in until the child is well

yes.chronicle: The child recovered, and the family went on their way in the spring.

no.chronicle: The child died in the guest room and was buried in the brothers' field, under a small cross.

choices.chronicle: {When}, a family with a sick child was taken into the guesthouse.

choices.label: Bar the gate
choices.chronicle: {When}, a family with a sick child came to the gate, and the gate stayed shut.

title: Fever
text: {monk} has collapsed in the garden, burning with fever.

no.chronicle: {When}, {monk} fell ill with a fever that the medicine could not break.

yes.chronicle: {When}, {monk} lay three days in a fever that broke suddenly on the feast of the Holy Cross. The healer had no explanation.

title: The Cold Settles In
text: The cold has settled in {monk}'s chest. He coughs through the night Office.

choices.label: Keep a fire in his cell
He must bear it like the rest

yes.chronicle: {When}, {monk} took to the infirmary with a sickness of the chest.

effects.chronicle: {When}, black rot came into the potato beds. The brothers pulled up what they could save and burned the rest.
{When}, snow closed the pass for three weeks. No one came to the gate, and the brothers kept silence even at recreation.
